Class ArabicTool

java.lang.Object
net.murat.tool.ArabicTool
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable
public class ArabicTool extends Object implements Serializable
Character constants and transliteration engines for converting between a Latin-based keyboard layout and Arabic script (including Persian extensions).

The conversion is driven by two parallel tables: latinchr and arabicchr. The character at index n in one table corresponds to the character at index n in the other, so the ordering of both tables must be kept in sync at all times.

All methods are stateless and thread-safe.

  • Method Details

    • toArabic

      public static final String toArabic(String str)
      Converts a Latin-layout string into its Arabic-script representation.

      Each character is looked up in the Latin table and replaced by the Arabic character at the same index. Characters with no mapping are passed through unchanged. If a Latin character appears more than once in the table, the first occurrence takes precedence.

      Parameters:
      str - the Latin-layout text to convert; may be null
      Returns:
      the converted text, or an empty string if str is null or empty

    • fromArabic

      public static final String fromArabic(String str)
      Converts an Arabic-script string back into its Latin-layout representation.

      Each character is looked up in the Arabic table and replaced by the Latin character at the same index. Characters with no mapping are passed through unchanged. Where an Arabic character appears more than once in the table (e.g. Shin, Tcheh), the first occurrence takes precedence, so the reverse conversion is not guaranteed to be an exact inverse of toArabic(String) for those characters.

      Parameters:
      str - the Arabic-script text to convert; may be null
      Returns:
      the converted text, or an empty string if str is null or empty

    • getArabicchr

      public static final char[] getArabicchr()
      Returns the internal Arabic character table.

      Note: the returned array is the live internal table, not a copy. Callers must treat it as read-only.

      Returns:
      the Arabic character table, index-aligned with getLatinchr()
